sections.h2: Where is Elkhart County and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Elkhart County sits in northern Indiana on the Michigan line, in the area people call Michiana. Goshen is the county seat, and Elkhart is the largest city. The county covers about 468 square miles, roughly 20 miles east of South Bend and 150 miles north of Indianapolis.

Six incorporated places share the map: Elkhart, Goshen, Middlebury, Nappanee, Bristol and Wakarusa. Smaller communities such as Dunlap, Jimtown, New Paris, Simonton Lake and Vistula sit outside any city limits. The county borders seven others, including Cass and St. Joseph counties in Michigan, so it is one of the few places in the country that touches two counties of the same name in different states.

Water shapes the layout. The St. Joseph River is the main waterway. The Elkhart River enters east of Millersburg, passes through Goshen and Dunlap, and joins the St. Joseph in the city of Elkhart. A house near either river or on Simonton Lake carries different drainage and insurance questions than a farm parcel near Nappanee.

sections.h2: What does the RV industry mean for Elkhart County home sellers?
sections.html:
The recreational vehicle business is the biggest swing factor in the county's household budgets. Elkhart County is known as the RV Capital of the World, and the city of Elkhart opened its first RV factory in 1934. By 1949 the city was already using that nickname.

A 2016 Indianapolis Business Journal report put numbers on the swings. Manufacturing, which covers RV makers and their suppliers, held 49.6% of county jobs in April 2006 (66,300 of 133,500). By April 2009 the share was 38.4% (37,000 of 96,200). By April 2016 it had climbed back to 46% (57,900 of 125,800). Unemployment peaked at 18.9% in March 2009 and stood at 3.9% in April 2016. These figures are a decade old, so treat them as a picture of the pattern and not a current reading.

An Indiana University economist quoted in that report described the county economy as resting on an essentially discretionary product. Local officials said many suppliers had diversified, though efforts to bring in non-RV employers had limited success.

Other employers fill in the picture. Elkhart is also known for band instruments, and it hosts Elkhart Brass, which makes fire-fighting equipment, and NIBCO, a flow control manufacturer. Norfolk Southern has the largest rail presence in the city. Goshen's industry centers on RV and automotive work, with names such as Benteler, Supreme, Dutchmen, Forest River and Keystone. When hours drop at a plant, a property tax installment is one of the first bills to slip, which is how many owners here end up selling with taxes due.

sections.h2: How is property tax set in Elkhart County?
sections.html:
Indiana splits the job among several county offices, and Elkhart County follows that pattern. The assessor sets values and hears appeals. The auditor applies tax cap credits to each bill. The treasurer sends bills and collects payment. Rates come from the local taxing units on your parcel, such as the county, a city or town, and a school corporation.

The state's circuit breaker caps limit the bill as a share of gross assessed value. They do not change the local tax rate. If a homestead with a $100,000 gross assessed value would owe $2,100, the auditor credits $1,100 and the owner pays $1,000.

Property classCap on tax as share of gross assessed value
Homestead1%
Other residential, including rentals2%
Agricultural land2%
Nonresidential and personal property3%

To get the 1% homestead cap you must hold the homestead standard deduction. A homestead covers the dwelling, a garage and up to one acre of surrounding land. For the many rural lots in Elkhart County that run larger than an acre, the extra land falls into the 2% class. The state posts each county's budget order every January, and Elkhart County's 2026 order was issued January 15, 2026 on the state's county page.

sections.h2: How does the county reassess houses?
sections.html:
Elkhart County reviews roughly a quarter of its parcels each year, so a different set of townships gets a fresh look every cycle. The assessor's 2025 ratio study narrative describes the 2024 phase. Baugo, Benton and Cleveland townships had residential and agricultural property reviewed, Concord had most districts reviewed in all classes, and York had commercial and exempt parcels reviewed.

The study used sales from January 1 to December 31, 2024. It treats improved residential property one township at a time because each had enough sales. The county calls itself heavily industrialized and values industrial improved property as a single countywide group. A land order was sent to the county board on December 3, 2024 and took effect January 1, 2025.

  • Each sales disclosure form is checked through phone contacts, aerial maps, field visits, MLS records and CoStar.
  • Interiors are not entered routinely. They are updated through questionnaires, talks with owners and listings.
  • Permits for all trades go into the county's assessment system. Elkhart, Goshen and Nappanee process their own permits, and the county handles the rest.
  • A remodel with a permit raises the effective age credit of a house, so work done before a sale can show up in the next value.

sections.h2: How do I appeal an Elkhart County assessment?
sections.html:
You file a Form 130 with the county assessor, one form per parcel. The deadline is June 15. Which June 15 depends on when the Form 11 assessment notice was mailed: if it went out before May 1, the deadline falls in that assessment year, and if it was mailed on or after May 1, the deadline falls in the year the tax bill is mailed. If no notice was sent, the tax bill counts as the notice.

After filing, the assessor schedules an informal meeting to compare information. The county Property Tax Assessment Board of Appeals must then hold a hearing within 180 days of your filing, and it must give you at least 30 days of written notice. A continuance request needs good cause and must be filed at least 10 days ahead. Skipping the hearing without a request can bring a $50 penalty.

If you disagree with the result, or the board says nothing within 180 days, you can file Form 131 with the Indiana Board of Tax Review. Further review goes to the Indiana Tax Court and then the Indiana Supreme Court. While an appeal is pending you may pay on the prior year's assessment without penalty. If you pay less than that amount, the unpaid part is delinquent. The state's appeals fact sheet lays out each step.

sections.h2: What happens if I sell an Elkhart County house with tax due?
sections.html:
Unpaid property tax does not block a sale, but the title company will require it to be settled at closing. The county's tax lien attaches to the parcel, so it is paid from the sale proceeds ahead of the seller's share.

The state's penalty rules explain why waiting costs more. Under Indiana Code 6-1.1-37-10, a late payment draws a 5% penalty if it comes within 30 days of the due date and the parcel has no earlier delinquency. In other cases the penalty is 10%. A further 10% of the unpaid principal is added the day after each later installment date. The extra 10% applies only to the tax itself, so it does not compound on earlier penalties. Payments go first to the tax and then to penalties.

  • Ask the treasurer for a current payoff before you list or accept an offer.
  • Ask the title company whether spring and fall installments are both included in the payoff.
  • File the sales disclosure form that Indiana requires with the county. Under a state memo written for the 2021 filing year, a sale that closes by December 31 can qualify the buyer for a homestead deduction the following year, and a disclosure form can serve as the application.
  • Check the memo's dates against the current year, since filing deadlines can shift.

Elkhart County treasurer information, office hours and due dates are on the guide above, so confirm any figure with the office before you rely on it.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about weather and flooding here?
sections.html:
Northern Indiana weather is harder on roofs and basements than the average Midwest address. Goshen's averages run from a January low near 17 degrees to a July high near 85. Record lows reached minus 24 in January 1984 and the record high was 102 in June 1988. In the city of Elkhart, snowfall averages about 74 inches a year.

Flooding has a recorded history. In February 2018 the Elkhart River in Goshen rose to a record 13.2 feet after heavy rain and snowmelt. More than 300 structures were damaged and some residents had to evacuate. The city later set stormwater goals and a plan to grow its tree canopy by 45%.

Tornadoes are part of the record too. On April 11, 1965, storms hit the area, and Elkhart County recorded 55 of the 137 storm deaths in the state. A buyer's inspector will look for roof age, sump pumps and drainage grading, and sellers who have repaired water damage should keep the paperwork.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and neighborhoods affect a sale?
sections.html:
Buyers and sellers in Elkhart County usually name the school corporation before they name a street. Elkhart Community Schools serves most of the city of Elkhart. Concord Community Schools covers the southeast side of Elkhart and northwest Goshen, and Baugo Community Schools covers the southwest side. Goshen Community Schools serves most of Goshen, with small parts covered by Middlebury, Concord and WaNee.

  • The Indiana Toll Road runs along the northern edge, with exits at Elkhart, Bristol and Middlebury.
  • U.S. 20 follows the southern edge of Elkhart as the St. Joseph Valley Parkway. U.S. 6, 33 and 131 also cross the county.
  • Amtrak's Lake Shore Limited and Capitol Limited stop at Elkhart, and the Interurban Trolley connects Goshen, Elkhart and Dunlap.
  • South Bend International is the nearest commercial airport, about 36 miles from Goshen.

Historic areas matter for older houses. Goshen's historic district, listed on the National Register in 1983, centers on the county courthouse. Elkhart lists historic districts along Beardsley Avenue, Morehous and State Street. Rural parcels, including those in Amish communities, often have wells and septic systems that need their own inspection.

faqs.q: Who do I call about property tax in Elkhart County?
faqs.a: Start with the county treasurer for bills and payments and the county assessor for values and appeals. The treasurer's office is in the county building in Goshen, and the due dates and hours appear in the guide above. The state also runs an information center at 1-800-457-8283 for general property tax questions.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to appeal an assessment in Elkhart County?
faqs.a: The deadline is June 15, filed on Form 130 with the county assessor. The year depends on when the Form 11 notice was mailed, before or after May 1. File a separate petition for each parcel.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Elkhart County house if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays the unpaid tax and penalties from your proceeds at closing, so the amount comes off what you receive. Get a payoff figure from the treasurer first so you know the number.

faqs.q: Why did my Elkhart County bill change when my value went up?
faqs.a: The circuit breaker caps limit the bill to 1% of gross assessed value for a homestead, 2% for other residential and farmland, and 3% for nonresidential property. A higher value does not always raise the bill by the same amount. If you have no homestead deduction you lose the 1% cap.

faqs.q: Does a flood or storm repair affect the sale of a house in Elkhart County?
faqs.a: It can. Buyers and inspectors look at past water damage, so keep receipts and permits. The Elkhart River reached a record 13.2 feet in February 2018, and local drainage and basement history is part of most inspections.

faqs.q: How is Elkhart County different from nearby St. Joseph County?
faqs.a: Elkhart County has Goshen as seat, a heavier RV manufacturing base and a large Amish and Mennonite population of 11,006. Its tax rules come from the same Indiana law, so caps and appeal deadlines match.
